content: The text provided appears to be a list of references from various studies, guidelines, and reviews related to tuberculosis (TB), its prevention, treatment, and management, particularly in children, adolescents, and individuals living with HIV. 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) has published guidelines on tuberculosis prevention, including recommendations for preventive treatment. These guidelines are accessible through their official repository and were last accessed on December 1, 2021. 2. A meta-analysis conducted by Colditz GA, Brewer TF, Berkey CS, and colleagues in 1994 evaluated the efficacy of the Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine in preventing tuberculosis. The findings were published in JAMA, highlighting the vaccine's protective effects. 3. Blok L, Sahu S, Creswell J, and collaborators performed a comparative meta-analysis of tuberculosis contact investigation interventions across 11 high-burden countries. Their work, published in PLoS One in 2015, provides insights into the effectiveness of these interventions. 4. The WHO released a position paper in February 2018 on the use of BCG vaccines, emphasizing their role in TB prevention. This document is available in the WHO's digital repository and was accessed on December 1, 2021. 5. Prentice S, Nassanga B, Webb EL, and colleagues conducted a randomized controlled trial in Uganda to investigate the non-specific effects of the BCG vaccine on neonatal susceptibility to other infectious diseases. Their findings were published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2021. 6. The WHO published an information sheet in 2012 detailing the observed rates of vaccine reactions associated with the BCG vaccine. This document provides critical data for healthcare providers and policymakers. 7. Hesseling AC, Johnson LF, Jaspan H, and colleagues reviewed cases of disseminated BCG disease in HIV-infected South African infants. Their findings, published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2009, underscore the risks associated with BCG vaccination in immunocompromised populations. 8. Cuello-Garcia CA, Perez-Gaxiola G, and Jimenez Gutierrez C reviewed treatment options for BCG-induced disease in children. Their systematic review, published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2013, provides evidence-based recommendations. 9. Hesseling AC, Rabie H, Marais BJ, and collaborators examined BCG vaccine-induced disease in both HIV-infected and uninfected children. Their study, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2006, highlights the differential risks based on HIV status. 10. Venkataraman A, Yusuff M, Liebeschuetz S, and colleagues analyzed the management and outcomes of adverse reactions to the BCG vaccine. Their findings, published in Vaccine in 2015, offer guidance for clinicians handling such cases. 11. Curtis N, Sparrow A, Ghebreyesus TA, and Netea MG explored the potential role of BCG vaccination in mitigating the impact of COVID-19. Their commentary, published in The Lancet in 2020, discusses the vaccine's off-target effects. 12. Fritschi N, Curtis N, and Ritz N reviewed the specific, cross-mycobacterial, and off-target effects of the BCG vaccine and new TB vaccines. Their work, published in Pediatric Respiratory Reviews in 2020, provides a comprehensive overview of vaccine impacts. 13. Marais BJ, Seddon JA, Detjen AK, and colleagues highlighted the global health threat posed by interrupted BCG vaccination programs. Their commentary, published in The Lancet Respiratory Medicine in 2016, emphasizes the need for sustained immunization efforts. 14. Kontturi A, Santiago B, Tebruegge M, and collaborators conducted a survey on the impact of BCG vaccine shortages on immunization practices and policies in Europe. Their findings, published in Tuberculosis (Edinburgh) in 2016, reveal significant challenges faced by healthcare systems. 15. Du Preez K, Seddon JA, Schaaf HS, and colleagues examined the relationship between global BCG vaccine shortages and the incidence of TB meningitis in children. Their commentary, published in The Lancet Global Health in 2019, underscores the critical need for vaccine availability. 16. Cernuschi T, Malvolti S, Nickels E, and Friede M assessed the global demand and supply balance of the BCG vaccine. Their analysis, published in Vaccine in 2018, provides insights into the challenges of vaccine distribution. 17. The WHO released a scientific brief in April 2020 discussing the relationship between BCG vaccination and COVID-19. This document is available in the WHO's digital repository and was accessed on December 1, 2021. 18. Dodd PJ, Prendergast AJ, Beecroft C, and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the impact of HIV and antiretroviral therapy on TB risk in children. Their findings, published in Thorax in 2017, provide critical insights into TB prevention in this population. 19. Ford N, Matteelli A, Shubber Z, and collaborators reviewed the role of TB as a cause of hospitalization and in-hospital mortality among people living with HIV. Their systematic review, published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2016, highlights the burden of TB in this population. 20. Badje A, Moh R, Gabillard D, and colleagues evaluated the long-term effects of isoniazid preventive therapy on mortality risk in HIV-infected adults with high CD4 counts. Their study, published in The Lancet Global Health in 2017, provides evidence for the benefits of preventive therapy. 21. The WHO published guidelines for intensified TB case-finding and isoniazid preventive therapy for people living with HIV in resource-constrained settings. These guidelines are accessible through the WHO's digital repository and were last accessed on December 1, 2021. 22. Bruins WS and van Leth F conducted a systematic review on the effect of secondary preventive therapy on TB recurrence in HIV-infected individuals. Their findings, published in Infectious Diseases (London) in 2017, provide evidence for the effectiveness of preventive strategies. 23. Cotton MF, Schaaf HS, Lottering G, and colleagues studied TB exposure in HIV-exposed infants in high-prevalence settings. Their findings, published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2008, highlight the risks faced by this vulnerable population. 24. Cranmer LM, Kanyugo M, Jonnalagadda SR, and collaborators reported a high prevalence of TB infection in HIV-1-exposed Kenyan infants. Their study, published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal in 2014, underscores the need for targeted interventions. 25. Kali PB, Gray GE, Violari A, and colleagues proposed combining prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) programs with active TB case-finding. Their commentary, published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2006, advocates for integrated approaches to TB and HIV care.
